newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Clinton, Annan review U.S. arrears and U.N. reform.
newsitem.headline: Clinton, Annan review U.S. arrears and U.N. reform.

text.p: President Bill Clinton and U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan on Thursday discussed the painful issues of American arrears to the world organisation as well as forthcoming U.N. reform plans.
"The president saw a turning point in U.S. relations with the United Nations," a brief statement said.

Annan noted that the $819 million payment Congress was considering for past dues and peacekeeping operations fell short of the $1,3 billion owed. But he thanked Clinton for his government's efforts to secure repayment, the statement said.

Privately U.N. officials are rankled by the conditions Congress is imposing on the repayment which call for the abolition of a variety of programmes, a reduction in U.N. dues and a Congressional audit of U.N. finances, among others.
Annan, in part because of pressure from the United States, is drawing up extensive reform plans to be presented in July.

Clinton, after his speech to the U.N. Earth Summit, met Annan as well as several of his key officials, including Joseph Connor, the American undersecretary-general for administration and management, who is responsible for U.N. budgets.

The two men also touched on U.N. peacekeeping or diplomatic efforts in Cyprus, the Western Sahara and East Timor. They also reviewed the situation in Bosnia, the Congo and recent talks between India and Pakistan, the statement said.
